text:
alex: Hey all — I hit a weird Helm/ k8s edgecase. We conditionally create an ExternalSecret in some namespaces, but the chart uses envFrom: secretRef for the app. When the external secret isn't present the pod fails to start with a mount error. How do we guard the envFrom so the chart stays installable even if the secret is absent?

marta: envFrom doesn't support `optional:` so you can't just mark it optional like a SecretKeyRef. Two options: (1) use Helm's `lookup` to check for the secret and render envFrom only when present, or (2) switch to individual `env` entries with `valueFrom.secretKeyRef.optional: true`.

ryan: +1 to `lookup`. Example:(I pasted this in a quick patch)
```yaml
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace "my-app-secret" }}
{{- if $s }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: my-app-secret
{{- end }}
```
This way the block is completely omitted when the Secret doesn't exist.

alex: Nice. Is `lookup` available in our Helm CI image? We run helm 3.9 in CI AFAIR.

marta: Helm 3.5+ has `lookup`, so 3.9 is good. One caveat: `lookup` queries the cluster at template render time, so it depends whether you're doing `helm template` offline vs `helm upgrade --install` against a live cluster. For CI which runs `helm template` you'll need to mock or use the alternative.

nate: If `helm template` is required offline for CI and you still want safe installs, the `env` + `optional: true` route is more deterministic. Example snippet:
```yaml
env:
  - name: MY_SECRET_TOKEN
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: my-app-secret
        key: token
        optional: true
```
That will let the Pod start without the key, leaving the env unset.

alex: Good point. Our app expects multiple keys and we prefer the full envFrom map when present. Seems like a hybrid approach: `lookup` in k8s deploys, and `env`+`optional` for offline template/CI. Sounds messy though.

ryan: Another pattern is to render a small fallback empty Secret via Helm when absent, e.g.:
```yaml
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace "my-app-secret" }}
{{- if not $s }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: my-app-secret
  annotations:
    helm.redwood/manual-fallback: "true"
stringData:
  token: ""
  other: ""
{{- end }}
```
That keeps the envFrom block untouched. But it's a bit hacky and could conflict with ExternalSecrets controllers.

marta: Yea that can race if ExternalSecret creates it asynchronously. We ended up combining approaches for other charts: use `lookup` for cluster-deploy path, and `optional`-based `env` fallback in local/template CI.

alex: Ok I'll open a PR that adds the `lookup` guard around envFrom and also a small comment explaining the CI `helm template` caveat + how to switch to `env` optional in testing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-charts/pull/1234

ryan: pinged you for review on that PR. Quick check: make sure to `quote` the name correctly and keep indentation with `nindent` if you put it inside a container spec snippet.

alex: Will do. Thanks for the guidance.
